He had mesiras nefesh for me.

He had battles with the administrators of the yeshivah; they were opponents.

And he was always at war with them, Rav Motl, yes.

Then he remained sitting, yes.

Yes, certainly, yes. He wanted to take two Arabs; Rebbe Yisrael would go to Meron, and the Arabs would find him on the road,

And he was sitting on, on an iron chair—not like this, so heavy.

He got up; he... Rebbe Yisrael entered the house.

He got up and took the chair. He was, he was mighty.

He and his wife beat my wife with blows, murderous blows, so that she would get divorced.

I asked the owner of the donkey to give me the donkey to ride on.

Then he said to me: "I have wheat; I have it on the donkey."

And I could not—I was sick—I could not.

So he, he, he left me naked and took the, the clothes and went away.

Yes.

[This is something new.]

Then I cried out with such voices. Then I heard the, the sounds of the horses walking with irons.

Then I said: "Perhaps this is a salvation?!" And so it was; it was a salvation.

Two horses came, with riders, yes, and they saw me—that from the tears of my eyes,

the clothes were wet, all, all, all (not understood).

And they sighed over, over my condition. Then I said, I said:

"What, what can I ask of them? That they should get down and I should go on the horses?"

What? Then they said to me:

"What, what, what can we do for you?"

Oy, I told them—they said that they were going to the village,

and there they would say that I was fleeing from the army, and they had caught me.

"They must, must bring me to the village," yes.

And they went, and I did not see them.

Nu, they caught me and did not want to release me, but the officers—they did not, did not—we did not see them; they went. Oy...

And also I forget. I do not, do not sleep. I saw the horses; I...

They told me—they rode on the horses and told me that I should walk after them.

I said: "What? Horses... I, I, I am walking—I walked on all fours."

I did not walk on two; on the hands and on the feet, like an ani... like a... yes.

Nu, could I, I walk after horses? What is this?

And they, they sat on the horses and told me like this, that I should go with them. Nu, I went on all fours.

I thought they would already stop, that they would wait for me. What, what is this?

But I see that I—that they are standing; I see the horses. It...

Until I came—I saw the horses and I went after the horses. Afterward I stopped seeing the horses.

But I had a path, so I followed this path until I came to the place of the shepherds,

the animals, goats.

[And you were fortunate.]

Who can tell all this?

[You were fortunate that they gave you cream to drink.]

Yes, yes. Then I came, and I asked them to give me water to drink. I was parched.

Then they brought me a box made of, of wood, a large box like this, with leben.

Oy, it was a miracle. Had it not been for this, I would have died.

And I was supposed not to eat and not to drink, yes.

Oy, oy.

[Afterward some Arab came with a donkey and took you to Tiberias.]

He remembers. And an Arab came with a horse, and this horse was entirely covered with sores.

The Arab was poor, so he did not have a good horse.

Then I asked him that I should ride.

"What will you give me?"

I told him:

"You will come to Tzemach. I have a wealthy family there; they will give you a lot of money if, if you take me."

Then he, he took me, and afterward he regretted it.

Oy.

[Why did he regret it?]

He, he wants money.

[Ah.]

Perhaps they will not give him; perhaps I only want... yes.

[Good, he took you as far as Tzemach.]

Ah, oy. At any rate, they took me to Tiberias by way of the sea, and I came home.

[Unclear: And there—it was not there in Tiberias], and those who had gone on foot—

they related that robbers came and took from them everything they had.

Then they said: "Because they had left me behind."

They, they told my family that I had remained—they did not, did not know in what, in what place, in what...

I—and I came, oy.

And I had sores on my feet. I walked on... in mud.
